## Description

Pennate needle diatom (70–150 × 5–8 µm) of brackish and coastal waters. Its cells, stacked side by
side and joined along the raphe, slide past each other in a coordinated way: the colony stretches
almost into a line and closes again, like a carpenter's folding rule, in cycles of about a minute.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 2 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [sliding colony](../../mechanics/stalks-and-colonies.md) of up to 8 cells of ~70 µm (longer ones do not finish
dividing), with a common phase. Amplitude and period estimated with a gliding speed of ~5 µm/s. No
published µmax (general value).

## Literature

- Kapinga M.R.M., Gordon R. (1992) Diatom Res. 7: 221 (colony movement cycles).
- Schmid A.-M.M. (2007) (colony movement; cited in the data file).

## Not implemented yet

- Real cells reach 150 µm ([division limit](../../bugs/diatom-division-geometry.md)).
- The colony is not seeded in the freshwater drops (it is brackish).

## Unique and shared mechanics

The sliding colony is unique; [raphe gliding](../../mechanics/locomotion.md) and the
[frustule](../../mechanics/metabolism-and-nutrients.md) are shared with other pennate diatoms.
